finding.claim: DELETE /reports/:id removes the report without any authorization check because authorize() is called without await, so its 403 rejection is discarded and remove() runs regardless of the caller's grants (or lack of a user).
finding.source: Any HTTP client sending DELETE /reports/:id; with no session req.user is undefined (server.js:5).

trace.note: authorize(req.user,'delete',report) called without await; returns pending promise
403 thrown later inside authorize but unhandled, after deletion already happened

finding.guards_checked: authorize() grant check at server.js:9-16 is present but its result is discarded; session middleware at server.js:4-7 only copies user and enforces nothing; no route-level auth gate.

verdict.guard_found: authorize() at server.js:9-16 is effective only if awaited; its result is discarded at server.js:20 (bare call, no await, no try/catch), so the 403 throw at server.js:14 becomes an unhandled rejection and does not block remove() at server.js:21. No route-level auth middleware exists; the session middleware at server.js:4-7 only copies req.session.user. The only other file in the directory is server.js, so no session setup exists here.
verdict.reason: server.js:20 calls authorize() without await, so the rejection from server.js:14 is discarded and db.reports.remove runs at server.js:21 regardless of grants. Caveat: server.js:5 throws a TypeError when no session middleware is mounted (none exists in this directory), so the anonymous path only becomes reachable in a deployment that attaches a session (for example express-session), which is the expected setup for this code; the candidate's line-5 description is inaccurate, but the core flaw is real.

finding.claim: Unauthenticated PUT/DELETE requests, or requests for a nonexistent report id, throw inside async handlers; Express 4 does not catch these rejections and Node 15+ terminates the process, giving any client a one-request crash (DoS). Plausible: depends on Express version, which is not in the repo.
finding.source: Unauthenticated PUT or DELETE request, or any request with a nonexistent :id.
finding.sink: Unhandled promise rejection from async route handlers, crashing the process

trace.note: with req.user undefined, user.id throws TypeError inside async authorize
PUT awaits authorize, so the rejection propagates out of the handler
db.reports.get returns null for nonexistent id
DELETE: report.id throws TypeError on null
PUT: null report reaches authorize, resource.id throws TypeError

finding.guards_checked: No try/catch, no error-handling middleware, no async-error wrapper in repo; Express 5 would forward these rejections instead, version unconfirmed.

verdict.guard_found: No try/catch, error middleware, or async wrapper. The only gate is server.js:5, which reads req.session.user and throws synchronously if no session middleware is installed. No session middleware exists in the repo, so as shown every request fails with a 500 before reaching the routes.
verdict.reason: The crash path needs req.session to exist (server.js:5), and nothing in the repo sets it, so the routes are unreachable as shown; whether an external session middleware exists is unknowable from this code. The trace also misstates server.js:26, which only fetches the report, while the null reaches authorize at server.js:27. It misses the stronger issue at server.js:20: authorize is not awaited, so a DELETE by an unauthorized or anonymous caller still runs remove at server.js:21 and its 403 rejection is unhandled, crashing Node 15+ regardless of Express version. That path is a missing-await authorization bypass, not just a version-dependent DoS.

finding.claim: PUT /reports/:id passes the entire request body to db.reports.update, so any client with write on a report can set arbitrary fields (owner, ACL/grant fields, id, status) beyond what the write grant intends. Plausible: real impact depends on the db schema, which is not in the repo.
finding.source: JSON body req.body (server.js:3) from any user holding the write grant on the report.

trace.note: await authorize(user,'write',report) checks action on the report, not on fields
entire req.body written to the update with no field allowlist

finding.guards_checked: write grant check at server.js:27 is correct and awaited; no field allowlist or schema validation on req.body anywhere in the repo.

verdict.guard_found: The write check at server.js:27 (`await authorize(req.user, "write", report)`) is awaited and throws a 403 on failure (server.js:9-16), so it blocks non-writers. No field allowlist, schema validation, or pick/omit of req.body exists anywhere in server.js (line 28 passes req.body unfiltered). db.reports.update is not in the repo, so any filtering inside it cannot be checked.
verdict.reason: The trace matches the code (server.js:25-28), the write check at server.js:27 is awaited and enforced, and nothing at server.js:28 filters req.body, so a user holding write can send any field. Whether that exceeds the grant's intent (owner, ACL, id, status) and whether db.reports.update honors those keys depends on the schema and update layer, which are not in the repo.
